note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a MHL 403; A06b MHL 403; L05 MHL 406): ordinary naturalisation after 10 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: Citizenship Act 1984, 43 MIRC Ch. 4 (Nitijela, Office of the Legislative Counsel), §403(2); Citizenship Act 1984, §406; Constitution of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Article XI §1(2). Every figure the file holds now rests on it, and the dataset is no longer cited. Loss isn't automatic: under § 406 the citizen is subject to loss for cause on the Minister's application to the High Court, and the Cabinet may approve keeping both.

sources.title: Citizenship Act 1984, 43 MIRC Ch. 4 (Nitijela, Office of the Legislative Counsel), §403(2)
sources.said: (a) was (on the date of the application) and has been, during the period of ten (10) years immediately prior to the date of application, ordinarily resident in the Republic; ... (i) subject to Section 412 of this Chapter, has renounced in the prescribed manner any other citizenship which he may possess;

sources.title: Citizenship Act 1984, §406
sources.said: A person who has reached full age and is of full capacity is subject to loss of citizenship, after hearing and for cause, upon application by the Minister to the High Court, on the ground that he has obtained the nationality or citizenship of another country by a voluntary act (other than marriage), except with the express approval of the Cabinet.

sources.title: Constitution of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Article XI §1(2)
sources.said: (2) A person born on or after the effective date of this Constitution shall be a citizen of the Republic if: (a) at the date of his birth, either of his parents is a citizen of the Republic; or (b) he is born in the Republic and is not at his birth entitled to be or become a citizen of any other country.
